prerequisites: Adequate knowledge of Internet access technologies and network protocols.

learning_outcomes.text: Explain the fundamental principles of cloud computing, fog computing, and edge computing.
Explain the basic principles of virtualization and containerization.
Explain the fundamental and advanced architectures of cloud systems.
Explain cloud security concepts.
Explain the main Amazon Web Services (AWS) offerings related to compute, storage, databases, networking, and content delivery.
Explain best practices in design according to the AWS Well-Architected Framework.
Explain methodologies for developing and migrating applications in cloud and containerized environments.
Students will gain knowledge and understanding of the models, terminology, and characteristics of cloud computing.
Students will gain knowledge and understanding of virtualization and containerization techniques.
Students will gain knowledge and understanding of cloud architectures, from fundamental mechanisms to advanced and specialized ones.
Students will gain knowledge and understanding of cloud security concepts and identity management.
Students will gain knowledge and understanding of the main AWS services and how to use them.
Students will be able to configure and use AWS services through the console and practical labs.
Students will be able to design scalable, resilient, and secure cloud architectures.
Students will be able to develop and migrate web applications to containerized environments managed on AWS.
Students will be able to implement caching, content delivery, and load balancing solutions.

Students will be able to assess the most appropriate architectural choices and cloud services based on security, performance, scalability, and cost requirements, as well as to adopt the best practices outlined in the AWS Well-Architected Framework.
Students will be trained to communicate concepts and solutions clearly and effectively, describe cloud architectures and configurations, and interact with both technical and non-technical audiences.
Students will be able to integrate knowledge acquired in networking and distributed systems with practical expertise in cloud computing and AWS services.
Students will acquire the ability to independently explore new cloud technologies, assess their applicability in different scenarios, and clearly present the proposed solutions.

syllabus_topics: Technologies and architectural solutions for cloud, fog, and edge networking and computing
Fundamental concepts and terminology of cloud, fog, and edge networking and computing
Core elements and enabling technologies of cloud computing
Introduction to the fundamentals and development of Amazon Web Services (AWS) architectural solutions
Basic concepts and global infrastructure of AWS
Security and Identity and Access Management (IAM) in AWS
Compute, storage, database, networking, and content delivery services in AWS
Design principles according to the AWS Well-Architected Framework
teaching_methods: Face-to-face lectures supported by slide presentations
assessment_rules: The exam is passed if the grade is no less than 18/30. To pass, students must demonstrate sufficient knowledge of terminology and the ability to identify basic elements of a cloud networking system, their characteristics, and main data analysis platforms and techniques. To achieve 30/30, students must show excellent knowledge of all topics, the ability to analyze complex cloud networking systems, compare technologies for complex applications, and propose appropriate scalability and functionality.
bibliography: Thomas Erl, Ricardo Puttini, and Zaigham Mahmood. Cloud computing: concepts, technology & architecture. Pearson Education, 2019.
Materials (presentations, videos, and activities) from the AWS Academy Cloud Foundations and AWS Academy Cloud Developing courses.
